description: I’m working mom of 2 kids and have limited time to focus on challenge so Ive decided to do it individually.
summary: Outpost Whisperer is a browser game for children aged 7–12 in which the player is the AI of a lunar or Martian outpost. Five module characters (Breath, Watt, Shell, Sprout, Echo) ask for power, but there are never enough tokens for everyone. Every day (sol) the child chooses who gets power and sees the real cost of the choice: more shielding means less food or science. Storm strength comes from NASA DONKI space weather data. It addresses the challenge by making the trade-off the game, in plain language, with no account or download. It matters because children see the decisions behind a mission, not only the outcome.
details: The child completes missions (Training, Moon with 4 sols, Mars with 6 sols) at two levels (ages 7–9 and 10–12). Each sol the game shows the space weather (strength 0–3). The child shares power tokens over the five modules, commits the sol, and reads "Why?" cards explaining cause and effect. Three goals give up to three stars: survive, send the science target to Earth, and stay safe and healthy. A score and a local high-score list reward replay. Choices have real-world meaning. Shield tokens must match storm strength, food takes a sol to grow, Mars oxygen costs more, and strong storms and Mars distance disrupt communication. The game is bilingual (Dutch and English) and has read-aloud, calm-motion, large-text and high-contrast options. Scores stay on the device and only nicknames are used. Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, Canvas, Web Audio, Web Speech and localStorage. A computer search of token plans on random space weather confirmed every mission is winnable. Limits: radiation is a relative score, game values are simplified, and the game has not yet been playtested with children.
